name: Equal-weight combination of styles

origin.authors: Asness, Moskowitz, Pedersen; Fernandez-Perez, Fuertes, Miffre
origin.source_title: Value and Momentum Everywhere (Journal of Finance 68(3), 2013); their appraisal of style-integration methods (Journal of Banking and Finance 105, 134-150, 2019)

how_it_works.simple: Run several weak trading signals at once, each with the same weight, instead of picking the one that looked best.
how_it_works.analogy: Like a panel of judges: each one is often wrong, but they are wrong about different things, so the average verdict is better than any single judge.
how_it_works.precise: Standardise each signal across assets every month and average the scores with equal weights, then hold assets in proportion to the average. In commodity futures 1989 to 2017, five signals with Sharpe ratios 0.16 to 0.59 combined to 0.97; six methods that chose weights from past data did no better (mean-variance: 0.74). In AQR's data, currency value and momentum (0.34 each, correlation -0.42) mixed 50/50 to 0.63, and commodity value and momentum (0.26 and 0.53) to 0.71.

rule: Monthly, per book: z-score each ingredient signal across the book's assets, average with weights 1/K over the K ingredients chosen in advance, scale the book to a fixed volatility. No weight is estimated from our data.
economic_rationale: Ideas that win at different times average out each other's bad years. Equal weights avoid estimation error, which is large when Sharpe ratios are small.
why_it_might_fail: Only helps if the ingredients are not highly correlated and each still has some return after publication and costs. It also adds choices (which ingredients), each a hidden trial unless fixed in advance.

reported_results.source: Fernandez-Perez, Fuertes and Miffre (2019), accepted version, Tables 1 and 4, Panel D
reported_results.notes: Single signals: momentum 0.59, value 0.27, carry 0.35, liquidity 0.16, skewness 0.45. Optimised (mean-variance) 0.74; best alternative 0.85.

reported_results.source: Fernandez-Perez, Fuertes and Miffre (2019), accepted version, Tables 1 and 4, Panel C
reported_results.notes: Single signals: momentum 0.11, value 0.67, carry 0.41, liquidity 0.29, skewness -0.04. Volatility timing 0.45, not significantly better (p = 0.27).

post_publication_evidence: Fernandez-Perez et al. find equal weights unsurpassed in sub-periods and across asset classes; AQR's century study reports a commodity multi-style Sharpe of 0.77 after publication (RES-0015).

relevance.reason: The method behind both combined books proposed in RES-0016; no data of its own needed.
